ev.q: During 2010–2012, a total of 1,369 unintentional petroleum product release incidents were reported by seven states
NTSIP recorded 8,684 single-substance incidents during 2010–2012, of which 1,369 (15.8%) were petroleum-related.
Petroleum incidents resulted in a higher percentage of persons admitted to the hospital and deaths compared with nonpetroleum incidents
The second most commonly reported type of petroleum releases (296 [21.6%]) occurred in private vehicles and residences.
Forty-six percent of the incidents were related to utilities, private residences, or private vehicles.
Petroleum incidents were less likely than nonpetroleum incidents to result in persons requiring decontamination (10.4% compared with 21.9%)
analyzed 2010–2012 data from the National Toxic Substance Incidents Program

methods_quotes.q: Descriptive statistical analyses comparing petroleum and nonpetroleum incidents were then performed.
Percentages calculated using the number of incidents in each column as denominators.
